_doc: Shared heading-identity corpus — stage 3 entry gate. Read by BOTH
src-tauri/tests/heading_identity_parity.rs and tests/heading-identity-parity.test.ts.
The Rust renderer is not callable from jsdom, so parity is enforced as one
fixture with two independent runners (same mechanism as render-fixtures/phase1.json).
expectedSlugs is the CORRECT answer, not today's behavior. currentlyFailsOn lists
the faces that do NOT yet produce it. Both runners assert: a face absent from
currentlyFailsOn MUST equal expectedSlugs; a face listed in it MUST NOT. Every
defect is therefore pinned as a defect and the branch stays green. WI-3.2 deletes
the currentlyFailsOn entry it fixes, and the assertion flips to demanding correctness.
currentlyProduces records, per DEFECTIVE face, the EXACT output that face produces
today. Both runners assert a pinned face equals its recorded value -- not merely that
it differs from expectedSlugs. Differs-from-correct accepts EVERY wrong answer, so a
pinned case could be corrupted further (even emptied of headings) and stay green.
Both runners also assert the recording still differs from expectedSlugs, so recording
a correct output as the current one fails loudly instead of re-pinning a fixed bug.
WI-3.2 deletes a face from currentlyFailsOn AND from currentlyProduces together.
Both runners read ids from h1-h6 ONLY, never a whole-document id sweep. See the
non-heading-ids case for why.
Every value here was MEASURED against the live code on 2026-09-12, not inferred.
FACES — each defect is attributed to the layer that owns it:
rust            src-tauri/src/services/markdown.rs, via render_markdown -> sanitize_html.
Those are the SERVICE functions; this composition mirrors how the
export_html command builds its body at commands/export.rs:60.
DISAMBIGUATION: the IPC command of the SAME NAME,
commands/export.rs:19 render_markdown, does NOT sanitize -- its doc
comment says so outright. On the live path the frontend's DOMPurify is
the only in-process sanitizer, and ammonia first runs at export.rs:158.
Owns slug GENERATION on the canonical path.
toc             src/services/tocService.ts parseHeadingsFromContent. Owns the TOC
sidebar's own parser and slug generator.
tocOffsets      the `offset` field of the same TOC parse. Only asserted where
expectedTocOffsets is present.
exportCanonical src/services/exportService.ts renderMarkdown with the Rust IPC
RESOLVING. This face owns anchor PRESERVATION only -- whether the JS
post-processing keeps the anchor Rust already produced. It is fed
Rust-shaped HTML built from expectedSlugs, so it cannot observe a
slug-generation bug; those are attributed to `rust`. That is why
suffix-collision does not list exportCanonical even though a real
export of that document does emit a duplicate id.
exportFallback  the same function with the Rust IPC REJECTING, i.e. the `marked`
degradation path (plan decision A1). Not the path users hit.
NOTE: src/App.tsx:587 is the only export call site and it routes to
exportRenderedHtml -> renderMarkdown, so exportCanonical is the live user-facing
export face. The Rust-only export_html command, which preserves every anchor, has
no frontend caller.

cases.name: all-levels
cases.note: H1-H6 baseline (edge-cases-test.md EC-TOC-001). All faces agree.

cases.name: atx-control-alpha
cases.note: Control for the clobber cases: a non-colliding ASCII id survives every face. It was load-bearing while the clobber cases were pinned -- without it, a stripped anchor was indistinguishable from a parse failure. Now that WI-3.2 B3 has unpinned them it is the trivial baseline the clobber cases are compared against, and it stays so a future regression tells the two apart again.

cases.name: non-heading-ids
cases.markdown:
# Real Heading Body with a footnote[^1].
raw
[^1]: The note.
cases.note: Extraction guard. A VALID document whose non-heading elements carry ids: a footnote reference, a footnote definition, and a raw <div id>. Both runners must read ids from h1-h6 only. Measured 2026-09-14: sweeping every id instead yields [real-heading, fnref-1, raw-html-anchor, 1] on rust and [real-heading, raw-html-anchor] on exportFallback, so a whole-document sweep reports this correct document as defective. Also catches the inverse -- an id MOVED off a heading onto a wrapper still passes a whole-document sweep but fails here.

cases.name: cjk-basic
cases.note: CJK is preserved, not transliterated or dropped (EC-TOC-003).

cases.name: punctuation-cjk
cases.note: Mixed CJK/ASCII/digits with punctuation collapsing to a single hyphen.

cases.name: dup-cjk
cases.note: Two collisions is the most the current counter handles correctly; this passes everywhere. It is the case tests/cjk-slug.test.ts:47-51 already covers.

cases.name: suffix-collision
cases.note: The third heading's literal text already slugs to `x-1`, which the count-based generator had just handed to the second heading. All three generators emitted `x-1` twice, violating document-unique anchors; needs a third heading to surface -- two is not enough. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 batches B1 (toc, exportFallback -> the shared allocator in src/utils/headingIdentity.ts) and B2 (rust -> the taken-set port in markdown.rs). Recorded defect before the fix, on all three faces: [x, x-1, x-1].

cases.name: emoji-then-literal
cases.note: TS applied the `|| "heading"` fallback AFTER counts.set, so it registered "" and the literal `# heading` collided undetected. Rust applies the fallback BEFORE collision handling and was already correct. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B1. Recorded defect before the fix: toc and exportFallback both produced [heading, heading] -- a true duplicate id.

cases.name: two-emoji-only
cases.note: Same root cause, different symptom: the second empty slug became the bare suffix `-1`, an id with no base at all. Recorded in neither plan before 2026-09-12. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B1. Recorded defect before the fix: toc and exportFallback both produced [heading, -1].

cases.name: literal-then-emoji
cases.note: Order asymmetry, added 2026-09-18 (test-matrix ADDENDUM A, user-approved). emoji-then-literal covers emoji-FIRST only; an implementation could fix one direction and not the other with nothing to catch it. Measured 2026-09-18 against the pre-fix tree: toc [heading, heading], exportFallback [heading, heading] (DUPLICATE); rust [heading, heading-1] -- already correct, so `rust` was never pinned here and must stay correct through the B2 port. Lands unpinned because WI-3.2 fixes both TS faces in the same change; pinning a defect being removed in the same breath would record a lie.

cases.name: literal-suffix-then-two-emoji
cases.note: Defect-one x defect-two interaction, added 2026-09-18 (test-matrix ADDENDUM A, user-approved). The only input shape that exercises empty-base substitution against the smallest-free-integer search: the substitution yields base `heading`, and the collision search must then skip `heading-1` because a LITERAL heading already took it, landing on `heading-2`. An allocator that substitutes correctly but restarts its search at 1 without consulting the taken set passes every other case and fails only this one. Measured 2026-09-18 against the pre-fix tree: toc [heading-1, heading, -1], exportFallback [heading-1, heading, -1], rust [heading-1, heading, heading-1] -- the ADDENDUM left the rust value to be measured rather than assumed, and it is DEFECTIVE here (duplicate `heading-1`) even though rust substitutes before counting. B2 fixes it.

cases.name: fenced-hash
cases.note: UNPINNED by the Lezer parser swap (ADR-0012). tocService used to match ATX line-by-line with no fence tracking and invented a heading from code-block content; recorded defect before the fix, on toc: [not-a-heading]. `markdownLanguage.parser` emits FencedCode/CodeText here and no heading node at all, so the toc face now agrees with Rust and both export faces on [].

cases.name: setext-noncolliding
cases.note: Setext headings (EC-MD-002). UNPINNED by the Lezer parser swap (ADR-0012): the old ATX-only regex missed them entirely; recorded defect before the fix, on toc: []. `SetextHeading1` is now walked like any other heading node. Deliberately NOT named `title` so the miss could not be confused with the clobbering strip -- that confusion cost a round of measurement, and the separation is why this case stays in the corpus after the fix.

cases.name: setext-title
cases.note: Two independent defects were stacked on one input: tocService missed Setext, and the slug `title` was then stripped by DOMPurify on both export faces. Both are now FIXED, in two separate work items -- WI-3.2 B3 set SANITIZE_DOM:false per ADR-0003 B' (the two export pins), and the Lezer parser swap per ADR-0012 fixed the Setext miss (the toc pin). Recorded defects before the fixes: exportCanonical [], exportFallback [], toc []. Kept alongside setext-noncolliding so the two causes stay separable; that separation is what made the first round a partial unpin rather than a whole one.

cases.name: formatted-bold
cases.note: The fallback's marked renderer receives RENDERED HTML as `text`, so markup leaks into the slug: `strong-bold-strong-title`. Rust, toc, and the canonical export all agree on `bold-title`.

cases.name: inline-code
cases.note: Same leak via `<code>`: the fallback yields `code-code-code-title` (EC-TOC-005, inline code stripped).

cases.name: link-in-heading
cases.note: Three-way divergence (EC-TOC-005, links stripped). toc slugs the raw markdown including the URL; the fallback slugs the rendered anchor tag; only Rust and the canonical export strip to the link TEXT. STILL PINNED after the Lezer swap, and re-measured 2026-09-18 to confirm it: `HeaderMark` subtraction removes only the `#` runs, so `LinkMark`, `URL` and the link text all remain in the node range and the extracted text is the literal `[text](https://example.com) tail`. ADR-0012 records this as a Consequence, not an oversight -- heading-text extraction is our code, and inline-markup stripping (LinkMark / EmphasisMark / CodeMark) is the deferred successor work that owns this pin. Do not 'fix' it by stripping markup without that work item: tests/toc-lezer-parser.test.ts B10 pins the un-stripped text from the other side.

cases.name: trailing-hashes
cases.note: Closing-sequence ATX (EC-MD-001). The slug is correctly `title` on every face; what used to fail was DOMPurify stripping the anchor afterwards. Measured as a parse bug in round 1; it never was one. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B3 (ADR-0003 B', SANITIZE_DOM:false). Recorded defect before the fix, on exportCanonical and exportFallback: [] -- no anchor at all.

cases.name: leading-trailing-punct
cases.note: Leading/trailing separators trimmed. Same story as trailing-hashes: correct slug, and the anchor used to be stripped downstream. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B3. Recorded defect before the fix, on exportCanonical and exportFallback: [].

cases.name: clobber-title
cases.note: DOM-clobbering defense, now retired on this surface. DOMPurify's default SANITIZE_DOM removed an `id` colliding with a built-in document/form property, leaving `<h1 data-heading-id="title">` with NO anchor. Rust/ammonia always kept it, so this was a TS-vs-Rust divergence, not a shared security posture. ADR-0003 accepted B' on 2026-09-15 (SANITIZE_DOM:false plus the sanitizeExportFragment rename); ADR-0011 unblocked it on 2026-09-18 by removing `name` from BASE_ATTRS, and WI-3.2 B3 landed both together. UNPINNED. Recorded defect before the fix, on exportCanonical and exportFallback: []. The fragment is safe without the defense only because it is written to a file and never enters a live DOM -- the function name carries that constraint, and ADR-0003's `<form>` precondition is guarded behaviourally in tests/sanitizer-policy.test.ts.

cases.name: clobber-name
cases.note: Same defense, `document.name` / form property. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B3; recorded defect before the fix on both export faces: []. NOTE the distinction this case does NOT make: it is about an id whose VALUE is `name`, which now survives. The `name` ATTRIBUTE is a separate matter and was removed from the allow-list by ADR-0011 in the same change -- see tests/sanitizer-policy.test.ts.

cases.name: clobber-body
cases.note: Same defense, `document.body`. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B3; recorded defect before the fix on both export faces: [].

cases.name: clobber-location
cases.note: Same defense, `document.location` -- the highest-severity clobber target in the original list, though ADR-0011 measured that `document.location` is [LegacyUnforgeable] (an own property) and is NOT in fact reachable by named access. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B3; recorded defect before the fix on both export faces: [].

cases.name: clobber-forms
cases.note: Same defense, `document.forms`. UNPINNED by WI-3.2 B3; recorded defect before the fix on both export faces: [].

cases.name: tab-heading
cases.note: CommonMark §4.2 allows a Tab after the opening `#` run. pulldown-cmark and `marked` both follow it; the Lezer grammar in @codemirror/lang-markdown 6.5.0 does not, and parses the line as a paragraph. Adopting Lezer for the toc face therefore briefly made the sidebar drop a heading the export still anchored — four divergences closed, a fifth opened. tocService rewrites the Tab to a space in a parse-only, length-preserving copy, so no offset moves. This case exists to hold all four faces together on the shape: it is unpinned because they agree, and it goes red the moment one of them stops agreeing.

cases.name: crlf-doc
cases.note: UNPINNED by the Lezer parser swap (ADR-0012). tocService used to accumulate `line.length + 1` after splitting on /\r?\n/, undercounting one byte per CRLF line; recorded defect before the fix, on tocOffsets: [5] against a true 6 (EC-FILE-008). A Lezer node's `from` is a UTF-16 index into the source string, so it counts the `\r` and needs no terminator arithmetic at all. Slugs were never affected.

cases.name: crlf-two-lines
cases.note: UNPINNED by the Lezer parser swap (ADR-0012). The undercount ACCUMULATED: two preceding CRLF lines gave offset 4 against a true 6; recorded defect before the fix, on tocOffsets: [4]. Line numbers were correct throughout, then and now -- lines are still derived by counting `\n` only.

cases.name: lf-two-lines
cases.note: LF control for the two CRLF cases -- proves the offset arithmetic is correct on LF and isolates the bug to CRLF handling.
